definitions.explanation: The way something is done or appears.
Used as a suffix to indicate the first time in a while.

examples.japanese: 3{年|ねん}{振|ぶ}りに{故郷|こきょう}に{帰|かえ}った。
examples.english: I returned to my hometown for the first time in three years.

examples.japanese: {寝|ね}た{振|ふ}りをして{様子|ようす}を{窺|うかが}った。
examples.english: I pretended to be asleep and observed the situation.

notes:
Has multiple related meanings centered on appearance/manner.

MEANING 1 - MANNER:
・{身振|みぶ}り{手振|てぶ}り (gestures)
・{振|ふ}る{舞|ま}い (behavior, conduct)

MEANING 2 - PRETENSE:
・〜{振|ふ}りをする (to pretend to ~)
・{知|し}らん{振|ぷ}り (pretending not to know)
・{見|み}て{見|み}ぬ{振|ふ}り (pretending not to see)

MEANING 3 - TIME SUFFIX:
・〜{振|ぶ}り (for the first time in ~)
・3{年|ねん}{振|ぶ}り (for the first time in 3 years)
・{久|ひさ}し{振|ぶ}り (after a long time)

NOTE:
As a time suffix, it's often read ぶり rather than ふり.
